summary: This note covers the early statehood history of Mississippi. Elected delegates drafted a constitution and sought statehood from Congress, and the western part of Mississippi Territory became the State of Mississippi on Dec. 10, 1817. Natchez, a major river port, served as the first capital until the capital moved to Jackson in 1822.
one_line: Early statehood history of Mississippi, from its 1817 constitution and admission to the Union to the move of the capital from Natchez to Jackson.
key_facts: In 1817 elected delegates wrote a constitution and applied to Congress for statehood.
On Dec. 10, 1817, the western portion of Mississippi Territory became the State of Mississippi.
The State of Mississippi became the 20th state of the Union on Dec. 10, 1817.
Natchez was long established as a major river port before statehood.
Natchez was the first state capital of Mississippi.
In 1822 the capital of Mississippi was moved to Jackson.
The capital was moved to Jackson because it was a more central location in the state.
The move of the capital in 1822 was prompted by increasing population and anticipated future growth in the state.
